newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. chief urges halt to fighting in Congo.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief urges halt to fighting in Congo.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan called Wednesday for a halt to fighting in the Congo capital Brazzaville.
Clashes erupted there last week after government troops surrounded the home of former military leader Denis Sassou Nguesso in a crackdown on militias ahead of a July 27 presidential election.
"The secretary-general is increasingly concerned about the deteriorating situation in Congo Brazzaville and the rising human toll in this conflict," U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said in a statement.
"He calls on the parties to cease hostilities and promptly begin negotiations to settle their differences."
Annan welcomed the readiness of President Omar Bongo of Gabon to mediate and appealed to other leaders in the region with influence on the parties to assist in any way they could, Eckhard said.
The secretary-general had asked his special representative for the crisis in the Great Lakes region, Mohamed Sahnoun, to support this peace effort, he added.
